context:
1. Docker Compose templates: one per extension, each with PostgreSQL + extension
   pre-installed, health checks, and volume mounts for data persistence.
   Follow pattern: docker/postgres-extensions/docker-compose.{extension}.yaml

2. Shared test fixtures (tests/unit/platforms/conftest_pg_extensions.py):
   - mock_pg_connection: psycopg2 connection mock with cursor
   - mock_extension_check: simulates CREATE EXTENSION / SELECT extversion
   - mock_guc_setting: captures SET parameter calls for verification
   - Reusable across TimescaleDB, pg_duckdb, pg_mooncake test files

3. Extension conflict detection in platform_registry.py:
   - Add "conflicts_with" field to platform metadata
   - Warn (not error) when user benchmarks conflicting extensions
   - Document that separate PostgreSQL instances are required

4. Comparison report template: standardized output for comparing
   PostgreSQL baseline vs extension performance, including:
   - Query-by-query speedup ratios
   - Storage size comparison (heap vs columnstore vs hypertable)
   - Load time comparison

5. Documentation (docs/guides/postgresql-extensions.md):
   - Overview of supported PostgreSQL extensions
   - Docker setup instructions per extension
   - Compatibility matrix (which extensions work together)
   - Benchmarking guide with recommended comparisons
description:
Create shared infrastructure, documentation, and testing patterns for
benchmarking PostgreSQL extensions as first-class platforms. BenchBox already
supports TimescaleDB (the first PostgreSQL extension), and two more are
planned: pg_duckdb and pg_mooncake. This item establishes the common patterns,
comparison framework, and Docker-based test infrastructure needed to support
a growing family of PostgreSQL extensions efficiently.

This is NOT about creating a new abstract base class - PostgreSQLAdapter
already serves that role well. Instead, this is about:

1. Docker Compose templates for spinning up PostgreSQL with specific extensions
2. A comparison report template for PostgreSQL vs extension benchmarks
3. Shared test fixtures and mocks for PostgreSQL extension adapters
4. Documentation of the "PostgreSQL extension adapter" pattern
5. Extension conflict detection (pg_duckdb vs pg_mooncake share libduckdb.so)

anti_patterns.dont: add extension-specific logic to the PostgreSQL base adapter
anti_patterns.instead: each extension adapter handles its own setup

anti_patterns.dont: create a new PostgreSQLExtensionAdapter abstract class
anti_patterns.instead: each extension adapts at its own override points
anti_patterns.why: PostgreSQLAdapter already provides the right abstraction

anti_patterns.dont: merge Docker Compose files into a single file
anti_patterns.instead: keep separate compose files per extension
